advice.heading: What to do next
LOW: No known warning signs were found. This does not guarantee the content is safe.
Never share passwords, card details or verification codes.
MEDIUM: Verify the message through the official app or a contact number you already trust.
Avoid using the link or phone number in the message.
HIGH: Do not open the link, reply or share any verification codes.
Contact the organization through its official app or website.
If you already shared details, contact your bank immediately and change affected passwords.
INCOMPLETE: Some required checks were unavailable. Treat the message with caution.
Verify through the official app or a trusted number, or try again later.
advice.senderType: Banks normally send messages under their company name, but sender names can be faked. Verify through the official app or a number you already trust.

help.title: How to supply logs (owner actions)
help.ownerOnly: Turning a log on needs administrator rights and is always your own decision; ETIS never does it. Commands are shown as text only.
help.dns: DNS Client log: enable Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Client/Operational in Event Viewer, or as administrator:
help.dnsSize: Recommended: raise its maximum size so the export covers the whole period (bytes, at least 1048576):
help.firewall: Firewall log: in Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security, open Properties and, for each profile (Domain, Private, Public), set Logging → "Log dropped packets" and "Log successful connections" to Yes. The default file is %windir%\system32\logfiles\firewall\pfirewall.log (default size 4,096 KB, maximum 32,767 KB). Copy it as administrator before importing.
help.sysmon: Sysmon (optional): only if you already installed it with network connection (event 3) and DNS query (event 22) logging. ETIS never installs or configures it.
help.snapshot: Connection snapshots (optional, when firewall logging is off): run by hand, or from a scheduled task you create yourself:
help.privacy: Exported DNS and firewall logs are personal data (browsing history). Keep them private and never share them.
